A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmniDraft and contain readable methods, results, figures, tables and appendices A–D. Retained material can be matched reliably despite additions, relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original acceptance rates, speedups, training curves and ablations on GSM8K, MBPP+HumanEval, Alpaca and XSum, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds model-scaling, distribution-shift, cache-memory and cache-eviction experiments.

M1.justification: The core probability mappings, hybrid distillation loss and adaptive-drafting Algorithms 1–4 remain unchanged. Appendix D.5 adds evaluated bounded-cache variants with LRU or LFU eviction, a limited cache-management adaptation beyond v1's full-cache procedure.

E1.justification: The four datasets and underlying task domains are retained. Appendix B.6 adds distinct nonstationary scenarios: switching from GSM8K to MBPP+HumanEval during training and switching target models within an ongoing training stream.

E2.justification: New Table 14 evaluates LRU and LFU cache policies alongside no-cache and full-cache variants; v1 contains no eviction-policy comparison. Existing decoding and distillation comparators remain, and the model-scaling experiment reuses the direct-mapping speculative-decoding baseline.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce a Llama-160M drafter and Qwen2.5 targets with 7B, 14B and 32B parameters. Additional protocols switch datasets at step 1000, switch targets at steps 300 and 600, and restrict caches to quarter or half capacity. Cache-memory and normalized-growth measurements also extend evaluation; the original settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands analysis through model-scaling and memory-footprint studies in Sections 4.3.1–4.3.2, recovery after dataset and target shifts in Appendix B.6, and cache-growth and eviction-policy sensitivity in D.4–D.5. The original loss, draft-length, LoRA and adaptive-head analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions' Appendix A.2 specifies three runs with different seeds and reporting averages. v3 adds no documented change in run counts, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance testing.

E6.justification: Matched original tables and training plots retain their results, while substantial new findings appear. Table 3 reports 2.05x GSM8K speedup for Llama-68M with Qwen2.5-32B; Table 4 reports cache footprints of 0.501–4.569 MB; Table 14 reports 1.36x speedup for both quarter-capacity LFU and full cache. Figures 5, 6 and 9 add shift-recovery and cache-growth findings.

T1.justification: Appendix D.4 newly defines normalized cache growth as cache_size/training_tokens. This is a limited mathematical definition accompanying a new empirical metric. Existing method equations remain unchanged, and no theorem, proof or formal growth guarantee is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same universal-drafter, cross-vocabulary distillation and adaptive-drafting claims, including the 1.5–2x headline speedup. The added experiments support these existing claims rather than redefine the core contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations of the larger-drafter acceptance/latency tradeoff, recovery under same-family target switches, and LFU's retention of frequently used n-grams. Appendix B.6.2 also qualifies cross-family switching as preferably requiring a fresh cache. The original limitations section remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 4 newly identifies pympler.asizeof.asizeof() as the cache-memory measurement routine and gives exact training counts for that analysis. Appendix D.5 documents eviction rules and capacity fractions. The original hardware, software and training-hyperparameter disclosures in Appendix A are retained.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 53 references are retained, including the existing positioning relative to UAG, OSD, DistillSpec and SpecDec++. The Qwen2.5 technical report was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: New analytical subsections are inserted into Section 4.3 and Appendices B and D, with corresponding cross-reference updates. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain unchanged. Title capitalization and the preprint-to-NeurIPS footer are also updated.

P2.justification: The visual evidence expands through model-scaling, cache-memory and eviction-comparison tables (new Tables 3, 4 and 14), plus dataset-switch, target-switch and cache-growth plots (new Figures 5, 6 and 9). Existing displays are retained and renumbered where necessary, with ablation tables and appendix algorithms reflowed.

improvement.justification: v1 mainly supports online adaptability through separate fixed-dataset, fixed-target experiments and leaves cache resource constraints largely untested. v3 directly examines recovery after changes, scaling to larger models, measured cache memory and performance under restricted capacity. These additions substantially strengthen evidence for central adaptability and deployment-feasibility claims while retaining the original results. Actual on-device execution remains un demonstrated; the reported hardware is still A100 GPUs.
